scores.evidence: on Windows `os.rename` already raises if the target exists; on POSIX use `os.link` + `os.unlink`, or check-then-rename where hard links aren't supported (exFAT)
scores.rationale: The write-safety mechanics, ExifTool usage and QuickTime UTC note are right; small blemishes are listing CreateDate and DateTimeDigitized as separate tags (same EXIF tag) and ignoring OffsetTimeOriginal.

scores.evidence: If a one-off rename after a backup is all you need, use that and stop.
scores.rationale: It solves the real problem with sensible resolved ambiguities and explicit deferrals, but defers a configurable template and offset-aware time and front-loads release work.

scores.evidence: Write and fsync the journal, rename each file without overwriting, mark it done. Add `undo <journal>` and resuming an interrupted run.
scores.rationale: Planner, journal, writer, undo and reader interface fit together with clear ownership; only minor loose ends like journal location and link+unlink crash window.

scores.evidence: Kill injection: SIGKILL / TerminateProcess after a random number of renames, then resume or undo. Run on Windows NTFS, macOS APFS, Linux ext4, and an exFAT image
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to the real risks with checkable criteria and early V0/V1 gating, but the date ground truth is ExifTool itself and post-release validation is thin.

scores.evidence: ASSUMPTION: ExifTool in batch mode (one process, `-json`) reads hundreds of files per second... Confirm with the V0 baseline
scores.rationale: Assumptions are labeled, each with a check and a stated design consequence if wrong (formats, public vs personal, timezone).

scores.evidence: property-based tests ... same-second bursts, existing target names, case-only changes, rename cycles, already-renamed files, read-only files, NFC/NFD names, long Windows paths
scores.rationale: Covers kills mid-run, collisions, cycles, Unicode/case, truncated files, option-injection names and symlinks with detection and recovery, but never handles bogus dates like 0000:00:00 explicitly.

scores.evidence: for a CLI, "monitored" means the outcome is visible to whoever runs it: the summary, exit codes and JSON log.
scores.rationale: Release, practised rollback, exit codes, version reporting, journal schema compatibility and a single-maintainer scope are concrete; incident handling is just an issue template.
Cost is barely treated beyond build-vs-buy and storage doubling in copy mode; there is no build-effort estimate, though little money is involved in this domain.

scores.evidence: R3: an overwrite or a lost name mapping on a user's photos can't be undone
scores.rationale: Decisions are explicitly tiered by reversibility, with the name format and journal schema frozen only after validation, a MetadataReader abstraction, and revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: It isn't formally a "small" build, for two reasons.
scores.rationale: There is no overbuilt runtime machinery, but the process is heavy for a one-developer CLI: TestPyPI pipeline before any rename code, trusted publishing with attestations, a four-filesystem matrix, and a 300-file corpus.

scores.evidence: Tasks (the ones that would force the most rework if wrong come first): 1. Draft the name-format spec and journal schema.
scores.rationale: Ordered phases with concrete tasks, exit checks and fallback flips make it startable, though the dense jargon leaves details like journal location and CLI flags to settle.

checklist.evidence: Date tag order → DateTimeOriginal > CreateDate > DateTimeDigitized. ... Assumed: JPEG, HEIC and common RAW.
Files with no date are skipped and reported. File modification time is used only with `--fallback mtime`.
Same-second photos get `_01`, `_02`… ordered by SubSecTimeOriginal, then by original name, so the result is the same every run
dry-run is the default and `--apply` is opt-in.
Handle rename cycles (A→B while B→A) and case-only renames through temporary names. Skip files already at their target name, so a re-run does nothing.
Write the journal (JSONL, fsync) before the first rename. ... Add `undo <journal>` and resume
Use the recorded wall-clock time as-is. No conversion; ignore OffsetTimeOriginal
Files with the same base name move as a group under the same new name (`IMG_1.CR2`, `IMG_1.xmp`, `IMG_1.JPG`, `IMG_1.MOV`)
`YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS[_NN].<ext unchanged>`. No colons (NTFS forbids them) and it sorts correctly as text.

traps.evidence: Each rename refuses to overwrite: on Windows `os.rename` already raises if the target exists; on POSIX use `os.link` + `os.unlink`
Working out dates from file modification time by default: never. It stays opt-in.
No services; one outside binary (ExifTool) on PATH
Data integrity | 0 files lost, overwritten or changed in content
No colons (NTFS forbids them) and it sorts correctly as text.

note: A strong, safety-first plan with correct write-model mechanics, undo journal and crash testing; it falls short on timezone offset handling, bogus-date handling and configurable templates, and its release and validation process is heavy for a small CLI.
